title: Charles Schwab CEO: AI agents trading on your behalf need 'rules of the road'
key_facts: Charles Schwab chief executive Rick Wurster spoke on Yahoo Finance about AI-driven trading on platforms such as Robinhood and Coinbase.
He said an AI agent should only trade on a customer's behalf if the customer gives it the rules of the road and oversees it.
He called the idea of simply handing over the keys 'a leap too far' and 'risky'.
Schwab will soon launch Charley, an AI-powered conversational assistant that will not be an agentic trading bot; at first it can do administrative tasks such as changing an address.
Schwab's third-quarter revenue rose 17% to a record $7.17 billion, just shy of analyst estimates; adjusted earnings rose 29% to $1.69 a share.
Schwab attracted a record $190.4 billion in core net new assets, up 38%.
The company said full-year revenue and expense growth would be toward the low ends of its prior ranges.
quote_evidence: "I think if you have an AI agent that is trading on your behalf, you have given it a lot of thought. I think an AI agent should only trade on your behalf if you give them the rules of the road," Wurster said on Yahoo Finance.
But just handing the keys over, I think that, to me, that's a leap too far. It is risky."
The brokerage giant will soon debut Charley, the company's new AI-powered conversational assistant. It will not be an agentic trading bot.
why_it_matters_hint: A leader of a major broker sets out a cautious line on AI trading agents, as retail platforms add them.
event_date: 16 Oct 2026 (Yahoo Finance's article date; the interview date is not stated)
notes: Yahoo Finance wrote and published the interview itself (Brian Sozzi), so it is the source. The article carries a disclosure that Yahoo Finance has a partnership with Coinbase.
